ledger.note: 775: Srivijaya takes Tambralinga. The page says it was 'conquered by Srivijaya in the latter part of the 8th' century and the infobox reads 'Formed Srivijaya Empire: 775-969' (elsewhere 'possibly under the influence of Srivijaya for some time').

927: Tambralinga takes Lavapura. The infobox reads 'Tambralinga-Lavo-Haripunchai war: 927'; the text has Jivaka of Siridhammana (Tambralinga) 'took advantage of the situation to occupy Lavo', take Lavo's capital Lavapura and appoint his son Kampoch (Kambojaraja) as ruler, and Sujita (c. 927) as father of Kambojaraja; 'the 925-927 Tambralinga-Lavo-Haripuñjaya wars'. Lavo page (second page): ruler table 'During the wars against Haripuñjaya in 927, Lavo's capital Lavapura was captured by the King of Tambralinga'; text 'left it open to annexation by Tambralinga from the south in 928'. The lavo-kingdom dossier dates the loss 928 (and ends its own 806 keyframe in 927), so 927 is drawn here from the capture and the one-year offset is for lavo-kingdom to settle. Repair: the land is now drawn by the keyframe tambralinga_927.

ledger.note: 946: Tambralinga's hold on Lavo ends. Lavo page infobox 'Tambralinga vassal: 927-946'; ruler table Kampoch (930-946?) 'As a tributary state of Tambralinga'; the infobox then has 'Angkor vassal: 946-1052'. The year is the Lavo page's and matches the lavo-kingdom 946 gain. The Tambralinga page does not agree: 'Later in 960, Lavapura was annexed by Siamese from Ayodhya, who also shared a political relation with Tambralinga kingdom' and Suryavarman I 'devastated Lavo which was ruled by Tambralinga's prince Kambojaraja' (inscription K.1198, 1014); the Lavo page too says 'Tambralinga lost Lavo to Suryavarman I'. 946 is followed because it is the explicit date and the sibling carries it; the 960 annexation is not drawn.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks; named by lavo-kingdom (loss 928, gain 946 with counterpart 'tambralinga'), sukhothai-kingdom (1294 gain, c. 1300 loss, 'Tambralinga') and others; the Malay peninsula group (se-02) was the suggested owner of some, and this dossier was written in se-01-x because Tambralinga lies on the mainland (check that no second dossier appears under this slug). One page opened (twice): thin and internally inconsistent, the reviewer should treat it as a sketch. Not settled: (1) the page runs two chronologies at once: Tambralinga as an ancient state (2nd century to 13th), as part of the Srivijaya empire 775-969, as the Siridhammana of Jivaka and Sujita in 925-927, and as independent 970-1277; the dossier follows the infobox; (2) settled in the repair pass: the Lavo years are drawn 927-946 to match the Lavo infobox and lavo-kingdom (see the next paragraph); (3) 'Fall of Tambralinga: 1277' against 'Split up by Singasari in south and Sukhothai in north: 1278' and the Ram Khamhaeng inscription of 1283 (or 1292) against the sukhothai-kingdom dossier's undated 1294 gain; the later state is Nakhon Si Thammarat (suggested slug nakhon-si-thammarat; also thonburi-kingdom's 1767-69 rival regime); (4) the 1244 'largest extent' is not mapped; (5) Pagan's suzerainty 1130-1176 (Wyatt, per the page) is for pagan-kingdom to carry; (6) the successor 'singasari' has no dossier (se-02 owns Java); (7) Dunsun and the other isthmus polities tributary to Funan (named by se-01-a) predate this and are not covered. REPAIR PASS 2026-10-19 (reviewer: fail on keyframe vs ledger). Applied: (a) KF0 split into tambralinga_150 (150-926), tambralinga_927 (927-946, isthmus plus the Cliopatria Lavo 806 outline, 126,430 km2) and tambralinga_947 (947-1276), so the 927 gain and the 946 loss are drawn; (b) the Lavo end is 946 (Lavo page infobox 'Tambralinga vassal: 927-946', ruler table 'Kampoch (930-946?)'), the year lavo-kingdom carries, instead of 960. Disagreement, with the pages: the Tambralinga page has Lavapura 'annexed by Siamese from Ayodhya' in 960 and Lavo 'ruled by Tambralinga's prince Kambojaraja' when Suryavarman I devastated it (1014), and the Lavo page has 'Tambralinga lost Lavo to Suryavarman I' (destroyed 1001; conquest 1011-1014 on one reading). A later end than 946 is therefore arguable; 946 is followed because the Lavo infobox and ruler table (with '?') give it and lavo-kingdom is already written with it. If lavo-kingdom moves its 946 gain, move the 946 loss and the keyframe end here. Open for lavo-kingdom: its loss is 928 ('annexation ... in 928') while its own keyframe lavo-kingdom_806 ends in 927 and the Lavo ruler table has the capture in 927; here the gain is 927, so 927 is drawn twice (one year). The Lavo page's wording ('As a tributary state of Tambralinga') would suit vassal_start/vassal_end on both sides; both dossiers use gain/loss. Not done, with reasons: the Pagan vassalage ('Vassal of Pagan?: 1060 or 1130 - 1176'; body: Wyatt, 'this claim remains disputed') is not drawn, because the page itself calls it disputed and pagan-kingdom does not mention Tambralinga; the 1244 'largest extent' has no boundary on this page (the Chandrabhanu page was not opened: page budget); the 1277 fall stays, and the sukhothai-kingdom 1294 gain and c. 1300 loss with counterpart 'Tambralinga' fall after this state's end: they belong to Nakhon Si Thammarat, which needs its own dossier (Nakhon Si Thammarat Kingdom page: vassal of Sukhothai c. 1279-1298, of Ayutthaya from the 16th century, independent 1767-1769, province in 1782).
